newsitem.title: GERMANY: Luxembourg-OECD report should not be overstated.
newsitem.headline: Luxembourg-OECD report should not be overstated.

text.p: Luxembourg premier Jean-Claude Juncker said on Thursday a chapter on employment would be included in Maastricht Two, the follow-up European integration document.
"I am sure that there will be a jobs chapter in Maastricht Two, but one needs more than a bit of text to create jobs," Juncker told reporters.

Juncker also said that a report from the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development on Thursday, which contained forecasts for fiscal and economic convergence in Europe in 1997, should not be over emphasised.
The Maastricht treaty calls for would-be single currency participants to have deficit-to-GDP ratios of three percent or less in 1997.
Asked about the report, which forecast that Germany, France and Italy would achieve budget deficits of 3.2 percent of GDP in 1997, Juncker said. "I would not overstate it."

Juncker said he expected Germany and France to meet EMU entry rules this year and added that Italy, too, would meet them if efforts were continued. "Italy should make it if it continues its stability efforts," he said.
